aggressive_definition: Advanced-stage incident prostate cancer and fatal prostate cancer arising during follow-up among men free from cancer at recruitment.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: There was evidence of heterogeneity in the association of some short chain saturated fatty acids with prostate cancer risk by tumor stage (p<sub>heterogeneity</sub> < 0.015), with a positive association with risk of advanced stage disease for butyric acid (4:0; HR<sub>1SD</sub> = 1.08; 95%CI = 1.01-1.15; p-trend = 0.026).
study_design: Prospective EPIC cohort study of dietary fatty acids and incident prostate cancer, tumor subtypes, and prostate cancer death.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: 142,239 men from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition who were free from cancer at recruitment were included.
reason: Cancer-free men were followed prospectively for total incident prostate cancer, advanced-stage disease, and fatal prostate cancer. The reported 936 prostate cancer deaths provide the count for the fatal endpoint; the advanced-stage case count is not given.

estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text table evidence explicitly identifies this estimate as total prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There were no associations with fatal prostate cancer, with the exception of a slightly higher risk for those who consumed more eicosenoic acid (22:1n-9c; HR<sub>1SD</sub> = 1.05; 1.00-1.11; p-trend = 0.048) and eicosapentaenoic acid (20:5n-3c; HR<sub>1SD</sub> = 1.07; 1.00-1.14; p-trend = 0.045).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly for fatal prostate cancer among a cohort free from cancer at recruitment, qualifying as a lethal aggressive incidence endpoint.
